title: Saw-leaf Zelkova: Ancient Keyaki You Can Visit
meta_description: Keyaki, Japan's great timber tree. The Great Zelkova of Higashine, 16 metres round, grows in a primary school playground.
intro: In Japan this tree is keyaki, the timber temple carpenters and taiko drum makers reach for first, and the giants that survive tend to stand where nobody could cut them. Japan's largest grows in the playground of Higashine Elementary, on the site of a 1347 castle keep: 16 metres round at chest height, a Special Natural Monument, and the children are taught that catching three falling leaves earns a wish. In Haramachi traffic goes around another of the country's three great zelkovas in the middle of a junction. A Korean queen is recorded resting under the zelkova at Hwayang-dong in Seoul in 1882, in disguise, fleeing soldiers who had stormed the palace; it is about 700 years old. Leiden's are the first zelkovas ever to leave Japan, and Florence's has been measured three times in forty years, growing from 3.30 metres round to 4.40.
